assumptions.text: Standard crop coefficients Kc (initial, mid, end) to estimate water demand.
Monthly Kc profile: first month initial, second month intermediate, middle months mid, last month end.
Monthly effective rainfall with the simplified USDA-SCS formula.
Available water by texture (midpoint of the range) times root depth (1 m if not reported).
Share of fallow rain that stays stored in the profile, by texture.
Half of the effective rain the crop does not use is stored in the profile.
Irrigation covers 80 % of the crop's deficit.
Water resilience is penalized when crop demand exceeds 80 % of annual rain (40 points per 100 % excess, max 40).
ET0 rises 3 % per °C of temperature increase in the scenarios.
The frequency of days with Tmax > 35 °C under warming shifts with a 5 °C standard deviation.
A month has frequent frost if mean Tmin is <= 3 °C; occasional if <= 6 °C.
Yield drops with the crop's relative deficit: 1 - Ya/Ym = Ky x (1 - ETa/ETm).
assumptions.source: FAO-33 (Doorenbos and Kassam, 1979); unlisted species: assumption

assumptions.text: Each crop's income is multiplied by its expected relative yield in San Luis (low 0.6; medium 0.85; high 1).
A crop's cover and organic-matter contribution drop by half the relative deficit it suffers.
With irrigation, rotation templates are chosen as in a sub-humid zone.
Each unharvested cover crop has a relative cost of 0.08 income units per year.
Erosion exposure: fallow months weighted by the previous crop's residue, the texture's erodibility and the windy months (July to November).
Qualitative catalog attributes (tolerances, contributions, income, market).
assumptions.source: AgroOrbit catalog, to be validated with INTA
